about: The evangelium of the formulary “12th Sunday after Pentecost” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: At that time, Jesus said to His disciples: Blessed are the eyes that see the things you see. For I say to you that many prophets and kings have desired to see the things you see, yet have not seen them, and to hear the things you hear, yet have not heard them. And behold, a certain lawyer rose up, putting Him to the test and saying: Teacher, what am I to do to possess eternal life? And He said to him: In the law, what is written? How do you read? In answer he said: You shall love the Lord your God with your whole heart, and with your whole soul, and with all your strength, and with all your mind; and your neighbor as yourself. And He told him: You have given the right answer; do this, and you will live. But wanting to justify himself, he said to Jesus: And who is my neighbor? And Jesus, taking this up, said: A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell in with robbers, who even stripped him, and having beaten him they went off, leaving him half dead. Now a certain priest happened to be going down that same road; and seeing him, he went by. Likewise a Levite too, being near the spot and seeing him, went on past. But a certain Samaritan, who was on a journey, came up beside him; and when he saw him, he was moved with compassion. And approaching, he bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine; and placing him on his own animal, he led him to an inn and looked after him. And on the following day he brought out two denarii, gave them to the innkeeper, and said: Look after him; and whatever more you spend, I, when I come back, will repay you. Which of these three, in your view, was neighbor to the man who fell in with the robbers? He replied: The one who showed compassion to him. Then Jesus said to him: Go, and do the same yourself.
